title: Learning nominates a cathepsin role in lung cancer cells
summary: CoxBoost and elastic-net selection included CTSH in a seven-gene lung-cancer signature. Subsequent experiments in HCC827 cells found that reducing CTSH increased migration and invasion and reduced apoptosis. This supports a model-specific functional role after learned candidate selection; it does not establish a protective effect in patients, a treatment or an in-vivo mechanism.

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Learned candidate selection followed by CTSH perturbation and measured cell migration, invasion and apoptosis in one lung-cancer cell line.
evidence.unknown: In-vivo confirmation, broader cell-model generalization and therapeutic benefit remain unestablished; survival models were selected using validation-cohort performance.
evidence.ai_role: CoxBoost and elastic net nominate a seven-gene signature containing CTSH, which the authors select for subsequent functional cell experiments.
